skill.name: design-mobile-apps
skill.description: Design, review, and implement mobile app screens through the Sleek REST API, including screenshots, version selection, and native framework guidance.
skill.summary: Create and implement mobile app interfaces with Sleek projects, generated screens, screenshots, and component code.
skill.author: designed-by-ai

security_audit.summary: Most alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, code fences, ellipses, and ordinary API documentation. The skill does require network access, shell-assisted response handling, and a bearer credential, and its fallback exposes that credential through chat. Its declared single-host boundary also omits GitHub-hosted media and Iconify downloads.

remediation.issue: The fallback asks users to paste a reusable API key into the conversation.
remediation.suggestion: Use the device flow exclusively, or instruct users to set SLEEK_API_KEY outside chat. Never request or display the raw key.

remediation.issue: The declared allowed host does not cover all documented remote resources.
remediation.suggestion: Remove external assets and Iconify fetching, or declare every required host and explain which data each host receives.

remediation.issue: The skill recommends shell commands for API response storage.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer structured HTTP and file tools. Use fixed project-relative paths and request confirmation before overwriting existing files.

content.user_title: Design Mobile App Screens with Sleek
content.value_statement: Turning product ideas into consistent mobile interfaces requires detailed design and implementation work. This skill guides Sleek generation, review, export, and framework implementation.
actual_capabilities: Creates, lists, retrieves, and deletes Sleek design projects through documented API endpoints.
Generates or edits mobile screens from product requirements, references, images, and style directions.
Polls asynchronous design runs, cancels stale runs, and handles documented API errors.
Renders viewport, full-height, combined, and version-specific screenshots for review.
Fetches component HTML and guides implementation in HTML, React Native, or SwiftUI.
Selects active or pinned component versions and preserves matching icons, fonts, and navigation.
limitations: Requires a Sleek account, network access, and an API credential with suitable scopes.
Sustained generation may require a paid Sleek plan and consumes service credits.
Design generation is asynchronous and depends on the availability of the Sleek service.
Native implementations require adaptation and visual verification; the API returns HTML rather than native source.

use_cases.title: Prototype a New Product
use_cases.description: Turn a product brief into coordinated mobile screens and reviewable screenshots before engineering begins.

use_cases.title: Implement Approved Screens
use_cases.description: Fetch selected component versions and reproduce their layout, icons, fonts, and navigation in a mobile codebase.

use_cases.title: Compare Visual Directions
use_cases.description: Create separate projects with distinct style directions and present screenshots for stakeholder selection.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a mobile sign-in screen for [product]. Include [fields], [primary action], and [supporting links]. Show me the result.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with one clearly scoped mobile screen.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Small Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design [number] screens for [workflow]. Use [brand traits] and [color direction]. Include the required states and show every screen.
prompt_templates.scenario: Generate a coordinated flow with a defined visual direction.

prompt_templates.title: Refine an Existing Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Open my Sleek project [project name]. Update [screen] to improve [goal] while preserving [constraints]. Provide viewport and full-height screenshots.
prompt_templates.scenario: Modify an existing screen and verify the complete result.

prompt_templates.title: Implement a Pinned Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement [component] version [version ID] in [React Native or SwiftUI]. Match its structure, typography, icons, navigation, and screenshot precisely.
prompt_templates.scenario: Build an advanced native implementation from a fixed design version.

output_examples.input: Design onboarding screens for a personal budgeting app with a calm, trustworthy style.
output: Created a dedicated Sleek project with a restrained financial product style.
Generated welcome, account connection, budget setup, and completion screens.
Prepared individual viewport screenshots and full-height review images.

output_examples.input: Implement the approved activity screen in React Native using the pinned version.
output_examples.output: Fetched the requested component version, matched its fonts and icons, implemented the screen, and verified it against the reference screenshot.

best_practices: Use the minimum API scopes and keep credentials outside prompts, logs, and generated files.
Provide one clear style direction grounded in the user request or choose one Sleek reference.
Review full-height screenshots before reporting missing content, then verify native implementations against viewport images.
anti_patterns: Do not ask users to paste raw API keys into the conversation.
Do not judge a complete screen from a viewport screenshot alone.
Do not substitute component IDs, screen IDs, active versions, or pinned version IDs.

faq.question: Does this skill require a Sleek account?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires Sleek service access and an API credential with scopes appropriate for each requested operation.

faq.question: Can it work without network access?
faq.answer: No. Project generation, component retrieval, screenshots, and optional icon downloads use remote services.

faq.question: Can it create React Native or SwiftUI code directly?
faq.answer: It uses Sleek HTML and screenshots as references, then adapts the design to the requested native framework.

faq.question: Can it edit an existing screen?
faq.answer: Yes. It can target a screen ID, send revision instructions, and show screenshots of the updated result.

faq.question: How does it handle historical design versions?
faq.answer: It can select pinned component and theme version IDs instead of the active versions for implementation and screenshots.

faq.question: Does Sleek usage have a cost?
faq.answer: Trial credits may cover an initial run. Continued generation can require a paid plan and consumes monthly credits.
